topic: MIDI SysEx wire-size governance for the FL controller bridge
context: The bridge transports base64-encoded JSON without transport-level chunking or reassembly.
observation: Approximately 1000 final wire bytes are reported reliable, while messages around 2000 bytes were previously observed to disappear.
result: Protocol v3 enforces a 1000-byte final SysEx wire limit, rejects oversized host requests, replaces oversized controller responses with a bounded error, and bounds expensive step, peak, and plugin parameter operations.
source_method: User transport observations, source inspection, deterministic JSON/base64 wire-size tests, and focused unit tests.
known_pitfalls: JSON size is not wire size because base64, protocol header, and F0/F7 framing add overhead.
A response-only guard does not protect oversized writes or rollback requests.
Selected step fields can cause a page to return fewer rows than requested.
reproduction_steps: Serialize compact JSON, base64-encode it, add the 13-byte protocol header and F0/F7, then compare with MAX_SYSEX_WIRE_SAFE.
open_questions: Re-measure physical-loopback reliability on each supported OS and MIDI backend before increasing the limit.
next_recommended_action: Run rollback-safe live probes with controller build channels-v40 and retain the 1000-byte limit unless repeated measurements justify a lower value.
